title: What "the key" of a song means
summary: A song built on one scale, at home on its tonic, is in that key.

steps.title: The key of a song
steps.body:
When a song takes its notes from one major scale and feels at home on that scale's tonic, the song is in that scale's **key**. A song built on G major that ends on G is "in the key of G major", or just "in G". (This is a different meaning from a piano key.)

**Why it matters:** "What key is it in?" is the first question a band asks. The key tells you which notes will fit and which black keys you will use.

steps.title: Same tune, different key
steps.body:
Play a tune that starts on C using the C major scale, then start the same tune on G using the G major scale. The tune is the same. Only the key changed.

**Why it matters:** this is what singers mean when they ask for a song "in a different key": same tune, moved to suit their voice.

steps.title: The key of F major
steps.body: A song in F major uses these notes and feels at home on F.

items.prompt: Play the scale for the key of F major.
Play the scale for the key of G major.

steps.title: Move a tune
steps.body: Play a short tune you know in C, then try it in G and in F. Listen for the one black key each new key needs.

items.prompt: A song uses the notes G A B C D E F# and ends on G. What key is it in?
A song uses the notes F G A Bb C D E and ends on F. What key is it in?
Play the scale for the key of C major.
